kitDescription: Asuka: WILLE is a Wind MG Burst III attacker built around a 9-second self mode called Annihilation State that only her own burst opens. Casting the burst trades away 40% of her normal-attack damage in exchange for +46.8% ATK based on her own base ATK, +36% attack damage, and an instant 21% magazine top-up; if the team enters Full Burst while she is in that state she gains a further +30.97% attack damage for 10 seconds. While the state is live, every 10 rounds she fires also strike the two enemies nearest her crosshair for a small extra hit and apply Anti A.T. Field, a stacking Damage Taken debuff worth 0.83% per stack up to 30 stacks — which amplifies the whole team's damage, not just hers. Independently of the state, every 50 landed rounds trigger a large 471.86% bonus hit. When the state ends she fires Annihilation at every target carrying Anti A.T. Field for 6.62% per mirrored stack and the debuff is then consumed. That same moment triggers Emergency Repair: her belt is emptied, she recovers 3.77% of max HP each second for three seconds, her next reload is fixed 60% faster, and her MG spin-up cost is briefly removed.

redAssertions: S1a x3 ('fires on a 50-HIT counter', 'doubling the threshold halves the proc count', 'is ungated') — the blind's removedTimes() multiset diff attributes 448 timestamps to the 471.86 rider vs the ~147 (= landed rounds / 50) that the driver's slug+atkPct event filter counts; INSTRUMENT artifact of the blind's timestamp-collision-prone diff, not an override divergence (the driver's direct atkPct===471.86 event count is the sounder instrument and is green).

burst 'ATK +46.8% is a CASTER-ATK flat add' + 'all three self buffs are keyed to HER burst cast' — the blind filters buffApply by value≈46.8, but the engine writes the resolved FLAT ATK grant into buffApply.value and carries the percentage in the key ('2:burst:casterAtkPct:46.8'). RECON_ERROR: the driver's stat is exactly casterAtkPct as the blind demanded; only the reader is wrong (the driver's own W8 filters on key.endsWith(':46.8')).

S1b 'debuff shape: 0.83 per stack, 30 s, capped at 30 (structural)' — expects durationSec===30 (prose literal); driver ships 9. DELIBERATE and documented: the burst prose says the status is removed when Annihilation triggers (state end ≈ cast+9s), so 30s never binds. S2b's spec and the S6 blind override BOTH independently landed on the ~9s effective life, so the S5 assertion is the outlier of three derivations.

S2b 'the 100%-ammo dump lands at Annihilation time' (window 6-12s after cast) — the driver's fullBurstEnd proxy lands ~1s late relative to the true cast+9s Annihilation instant and can slip past the blind's upper bound. Documented proxy (no delayed/state-end trigger keyed to her own burst exists); the co-located S5 assertion 'she does NOT reload in the first second of her window' — the high-stakes burstCast nearest-wrong — passes.

S2b 'reload speed fixed +60% for 1 ROUND' (durationShots===1, durationSec undefined) — driver ships durationSec 10.5. Genuine semantic divergence: the driver reports types.ts has no round-count/clamp form for reloadSpeedPct, the S6 blind assumed durationShots:1. See gotcha 2.

gotchas.summary: The driver's unit-test docblock is STALE and now contradicts both the shipped override and the test's own assertions — it documents the pre-gauntlet encoding as if it were current.
gotchas.evidence: Header says S2 Eff2 'Removes 100% of ammo -> UNMODELED (see header note)' while W11 asserts consumeAmmo fraction:1 on a fullBurstEnd block; says 'W3 TIER-2 HEADLINE: trigger is `burstCast`, NOT `fullBurstEnter`' while the override ships fullBurstEnter + ownBurstGate 'cast' and W3's title says so; says W10 '(Timing: encoded at cast -> no FB major)' while W10 asserts `inFullBurst && fbMajorApplied` on a delaySec:9 hit; W5's header line says Emergency Repair is 'encoded at burstCast'. The W2 note also still describes the 15.62 rider as 'the steady-state proxy ... every 44 overall shots', the encoding the gauntlet replaced. Neither blind agent could see this file; it is a driver-only artifact defect.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Rewrite the docblock to the shipped encoding: S2 Eff2 = consumeAmmo fraction:1 at fullBurstEnd; W3 = fullBurstEnter + ownBurstGate 'cast' (nearest-wrong = bare fullBurstEnter, NOT burstCast); W5 = fullBurstEnd; W10 = delaySec:9 landing at state end inside FB, FB major APPLIED; W2 = requiresTargetStatus-gated hitCount 10, not a /44 time-average. The per-unit test header is the spec of record for the next auditor, so a stale header will re-introduce the fixed defects.

gotchas.summary: 'Reload speed is fixed at a 60% increase for 1 rounds' is modeled as a 10.5-second window, which at MG cadence can accelerate roughly two reloads where the kit grants one.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Reload speed is fixed at a 60% increase for 1 rounds.' Driver: `{stat: reloadSpeedPct, value: 60, durationSec: 10.5}`. Both blind agents wrote `durationShots: 1`, and S5 asserts `durationSec === undefined` (RED). Faster reloads mean more rounds fired, so this sits in the shot-economy damage path, not a defensive one. With ammo 300 at the engine's MG cadence a belt empties in well under 10.5s, so the window covers more reloads than the one round the kit specifies. The driver's justification (types.ts has no round-count/clamp form for this stat) could not be re-verified in this pass — no tool access.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Read types.ts and settle the primitive: if a buff round-count form exists, ship `durationShots: 1` per both blind derivations. If it genuinely does not, narrow the window to one reload's worth of wall-clock (~161/1.6 frames ≈ 1.7s from the forced reload) rather than 10.5s, and keep the 'fixed at / set-not-add' nuance flagged. Do not widen further to fit a total.

gotchas.summary: A SELF mode is represented as a fabricated status inflicted on the boss, which is an unguarded side channel any other unit reading target statuses could pick up.
gotchas.evidence: Kit says 'Activates only when in Annihilation State status. Affects self.' — the status lives on HER. Driver: `burst -> {kind: targetStatus, name: 'Annihilation State', durationSec: 9}` on `target: {kind: enemy}`, with skill1 gating on `requiresTargetStatus`. The driver documents the proxy and its provenance (marciana/privaty pattern) but not the contamination surface: any unit whose kit gates on this status name, or any mechanic that scales off status/debuff COUNT on the target, would now read a status the boss should not carry. Inert in the liter/crown/helm control comp; not inert by construction. S6 instead proxied the gate with fbGate 'inFb' + ownBurstGate 'cast' (no fabricated status, but a worse-fitting window).
gotchas.suggestedFix: Keep the proxy (it is the better window fit) but add the contamination caveat to the note, and grep for other consumers of `requiresTargetStatus`/target-status-count before this unit enters any comp with debuff-count scaling. The durable fix is a self-status window primitive mirroring requiresTargetStatus.

gotchas.summary: 'Affects the target(s) afflicted with Anti A.T. Field' — the finisher's affliction precondition is nowhere in the override: no gate, no caveat, no `unmodeled` entry.
gotchas.evidence: Kit header on the second burst block: '■ Affects the target(s) afflicted with Anti A.T. Field.' Driver's finisher block is an ungated `burstCast` + `flatDamage 198.6, delaySec: 9` with no `requiresTargetStatus` (the debuff is a damageTakenPct buff, not a named status, so there is nothing to gate on). The driver's note documents the STACK MIRROR proxy (⚑4/⚑5) and the consumption gap (⚑6) but never the precondition. Behaviourally near-inert in this fixture: the gated 10-shot proc guarantees stacks exist by cast+9s, so the finisher never fires against a clean boss.
gotchas.suggestedFix: One line in `caveats`: the finisher's 'targets afflicted with Anti A.T. Field' precondition is unexpressible (the debuff is a stat buff, not a named status) and is inert here because the in-window proc always builds stacks first. Note that it would matter if she ever bursts without firing in-window, or once stack-count mirroring becomes dynamic.

gotchas.slot: skill2 vs burst (two proxies for one in-game instant)
gotchas.summary: Annihilation-State end is modeled twice with different clocks — burstCast+delaySec 9 for the finisher, fullBurstEnd for Emergency Repair — so two effects the kit fires simultaneously land ~1s apart.
gotchas.evidence: Kit ties both to the same moment: burst 'After Annihilation State ends, fires powerful attacks' and skill2 'Activates when using Annihilation'. Driver ships `delaySec: 9` from burstCast for the finisher (S5 confirms landing at cast+7.5-11s) but `fullBurstEnd` for the repair package (FB start + 10s ≈ cast+10.5s). The ~1s gap is what makes S5's 'ammo dump lands 6-12s after cast' assertion RED. Consequence is one magazine boundary / one lastBullet, and the ammo dump landing after rather than at the finisher.
gotchas.suggestedFix: If the schema accepts delaySec on buff/heal/consumeAmmo effects, re-key the Emergency Repair block to burstCast + delaySec 9 so both proxies share one clock; if it does not, say so explicitly in the note (currently the note explains why fullBurstEnd beats burstCast but never addresses why the finisher got delaySec and this block did not).

verdictRationale: GO. Every load-bearing line in S2b's set is either FAITHFUL or a documented gap with a measurement recipe, and the two highest-value gauntlet fixes are independently corroborated rather than merely self-reported: S6 (blind, prose-only) converged on the SAME encodings for the S2 FB-entry gate (fullBurstEnter + ownBurstGate 'cast', not bare fullBurstEnter and not burstCast), the Emergency Repair trigger (fullBurstEnd), the consumeAmmo recovery, the 3-tick heal, and — critically — the Anti A.T. Field 30s->9s truncation, which S2b's independent spec also called for. That last fix is the real money: a damageTakenPct debuff is a target-side amp on the WHOLE team, and the pre-gauntlet 30-stack near-permanent encoding over-credited team damage by ~3-4x average (team sum 1979M->1837M). Convergence is mechanically RED, not green, and I classify all eight S5 failures as non-defects: five are blind instrument errors (the removedTimes multiset over-attributing the 471.86 rider at 448 vs ~147; two reads of buffApply.value where the engine stores the resolved flat ATK and carries the percentage in the key), one is the 30s-literal assertion where the driver is MORE faithful and outvoted 2-1 by the other derivations, and two are the documented proxies I raise as gotchas 2 and 5. Discrimination holds: each load-bearing test fails under its named nearest-wrong (ownBurstGate stripped fires strictly more; the gate-dropped counterfactual leaks 15.62 procs across the whole fight; the single-stack finisher reads 6.62 not 198.6; dropping the -40 lifts normals while leaving riders within 2%), and S5's independent delaySec assertion confirms the finisher genuinely lands at cast+9s rather than at cast. Ranked real findings: (1) the driver's test docblock is stale and still documents the pre-gauntlet encoding — a med-severity artifact defect that will mislead the next auditor into re-introducing the exact bugs this gauntlet fixed, and the only finding I would ask to be fixed before the next unit; (2) the reloadSpeedPct 10.5s window, the loosest proxy in the file, where both blind agents' durationShots:1 is plausibly more faithful and which I could not adjudicate without reading types.ts; (3-5) three low-severity undocumented-nuance items (the fabricated boss status as a side channel, the dropped 'afflicted with Anti A.T. Field' precondition, the two different clocks for one in-game instant). Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: all five agents in this gauntlet are the same model family, so convergence proves stability, not correctness — the two places where that matters most are (a) the finisher's 6.62 x 30 magnitude, which rests entirely on the engine's MG cadence profile producing >=300 in-window rounds (the driver's own test does show stacks hitting the 30 cap, so it is internally consistent, but S6's 10-stack read from a ~12 rounds/s prior is a 3x disagreement that only an ammo-counter read off footage can settle), and (b) the heal, whose activation no SimEvent surfaces, so both test suites can only pin it structurally and S2b's expectation that crown consumes her recovery events is NOT borne out in the sim. Packet bookkeeping: the driver section claims 27 assertions but the S2d run shows 24 tests. Also note I had no tool access in this pass, so scripts/kit-autonomy/results/asuka-wille.json was NOT written — the orchestrator must persist this JSON to that path, and the S5 RED classifications above are traced from the artifacts rather than re-executed.
